stem.en: Sort each wave by the way its particles vibrate, compared with the way the wave travels.

label.en: Longitudinal: particles vibrate parallel to the travel
Transverse: particles vibrate across the travel

text.en: A sound wave in the air of a room
A slinky pushed and pulled along its length
The first earthquake waves to reach a seismograph
A rope shaken up and down at one end

explanation.en: In sound, in a slinky pushed along its length, and in the first earthquake waves to reach a seismograph, the particles vibrate along the line the wave travels: these are longitudinal waves. In a rope shaken up and down, each point moves across the way the wave travels: a transverse wave. Light is also a transverse wave, but it needs no medium.

hints.en: For each case, picture one particle. Does it move along the way the wave goes, or across it?
On a rope the wave moves along the rope, but each point of the rope moves up and down.
